# Overview

```{r} 
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

In this activity we are going to practice how to collaborate using GitHub and Positron.  
With your team members you will work on sharing and editing files on GitHub. 

![](https://happygitwithr.com/img/watch-me-diff-watch-me-rebase-smaller.png)



## Getting Ready

1. Identify your team! Go to Canvas and find out which team you are in for Lab 1.

1. Find the other members of your team and sit with them.

1. Introduce yourself to each other. 

1. If someone is missing from your group, let the instructor or TA know.

1. Follow the instructions on [today's slides](https://ds2020-at-isu.github.io/labs/lab01.html).



## Join Your Lap Repo in Classroom 50

Accept the link to Classroom 50 shared on today's Canvas page.
  
  - This link will ask you to log in to GitHub. Select your name from the list by clicking on it.  
  
  - Accept Lab #1 assignment in our course.

  - Check if your team number already exists as a group.
    - If it does, ask the team member who created it to add you.
        - You can add members by clicking on your group and selecting "add members"
    - If it doesn't exist yet, create it yourself.
        - Name the team the same as it is on Canvas (e.g., team1, team2, etc.)
        - Add your group members that are here today (using their GitHub username)



## What You Need to Do

As you complete the following steps, take notes on the process. These notes will go into your file for a final commit.

1. If this is the first time you are using `git` on your machine, you can start with [chapter 7](https://happygitwithr.com/hello-git)
    * If `git` is not installed on your computer, follow the steps in [chapter 6](https://happygitwithr.com/install-git)

2. Open a [git repository in Positron](https://positron.posit.co/git.html#open-a-git-repository) from the existing git repository for the assignment
    1. New > New Folder from Git 
    1. In "Repository URL", past the URL of your group's GitHub repository. It will be something like this: `https://github.com/jennybc/myrepo.git`. You can find this under the `<>Code` button; just copy the `HTTPS` URL.
    1. Set the parent folder to be the folder you created for this class.
    1. Select "OK"

3. In Positron, modify the `README.md` file, e.g., add your name and some sample text ("My first commit!").

## What You Need to Do (continued)

4. Commit this change to your local repo. 
    1. Select "Source Control" in the left pane (looks like a branch)
    1. Under "Changes", select the `+` to stage changes
    1. Add a commit message above the blue commit button
    1. Select "Commit"
    1. Once your changes commit, select "Sync". This will push changes and pull new changes from others.

5. Confirm the changes by returning to your browser.

If you run into an error, describe it and the error message. As a group, try to solve the problem. Write up the solution.

Finally, collect all of your experiences and make it into one cohesive document. Use the `README.md` file of the repo for this document, i.e., there should be a list of all steps in above (#1-5), followed by a description of all the errors you encountered and your solutions. 



## Example `README.md` in the End

```
### step 3

- Will's note: 

- Craig's note: 

### step 4

- Will's note:

- Craig's note
```



## Grading & Submission

**Grading:** We expect equal contributions from all members in a team. For the grading we will make use of the github commit history to verify that everybody contributed. 


**Submission:**
All submissions to the github repo will be automatically uploaded for grading once the due date is passed. 


Due date: Monday at 5 pm. You have time until Monday at 11:59 pm to submit final edits to the `README.md` file. Make sure that there are no commit issues.
